question: What does the Basic Control Skills test primarily evaluate?
choice_a: Your basic skills in controlling a commercial vehicle and judging its position in relation to other objects
choice_b: Your knowledge of state traffic laws
choice_c: Your ability to complete a pre-trip inspection
choice_d: Your reaction time in emergency braking situations
explanation: The manual states the test demonstrates basic skills in controlling a commercial vehicle and judging its position in relation to other objects.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, Overview

question: According to the manual, what will you receive points for during Basic Control Skills exercises?
choice_a: Completing the exercise in the shortest possible time
choice_b: Changing direction to gain a better position, crossing over or touching boundary lines or cones, and your final position
choice_c: Using the horn at the start of each exercise
choice_d: Keeping all vehicle windows closed during backing
explanation: The manual states you will receive points for changing direction to gain a better position, crossing over or touching boundary lines or cones, and for your final position.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, Overview

question: Under what condition may you be permitted to exit the vehicle during backing exercises?
choice_a: Only if the examiner is also outside the vehicle
choice_b: At any time you feel unsure about vehicle position, without restriction
choice_c: To check around the vehicle during backing exercises, following safe exit procedures
choice_d: Only after the entire Basic Control Skills test is complete
explanation: The manual states you may be permitted to exit the vehicle to check around it during backing exercises, provided you follow the required safe entry/exit procedures.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, Overview

question: What three things must you do when entering or exiting the vehicle during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Turn off the engine, remove the key, and lock the doors
choice_b: Activate the four-way flashers, sound the horn, and open all windows
choice_c: Notify the examiner verbally, unbuckle your seatbelt, and check mirrors
choice_d: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral, and maintain three points of contact while facing the vehicle
explanation: The manual requires setting the parking brake, placing the vehicle in neutral, and safely exiting/entering by facing the vehicle while maintaining three points of contact.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, Overview

question: When exiting or entering a bus specifically (rather than a truck), what must you do?
choice_a: Face forward and maintain a firm grasp on the handrail
choice_b: Face away from the vehicle and hold the door frame
choice_c: Exit only through the rear emergency door
choice_d: Face the vehicle and use both handrails simultaneously
explanation: On a bus, the manual specifies you should face forward and maintain a firm grasp on the handrail when entering or exiting, rather than facing the vehicle as with other vehicle types.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, Overview

question: What happens if, while in physical control of the vehicle, you open the door or move from a seated position (or on a bus, walk to the back for a better view)?
choice_a: You automatically fail the test
choice_b: You will be scored for a look
choice_c: It is not scored unless it happens more than once
choice_d: You receive an automatic pull-up
explanation: The manual states that if you open the door or move from a seated position while in physical control of the vehicle, you will be scored for a look.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, Overview

question: How is a 'pull-up' defined in Basic Control Skills scoring?
choice_a: Backing up on a forward-moving exercise to clear an encroachment
choice_b: Stopping the vehicle without changing direction
choice_c: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Pull-ups

question: On which two exercises are pull-ups scored?
choice_a: Exercise 1 (Forward Stop) and Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)
choice_b: Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking) only
choice_c: All four exercises equally
choice_d: Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
explanation: The manual states pull-ups are scored on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Pull-ups

question: Are you penalized for your first (initial) pull-up on an exercise where pull-ups are scored?
choice_a: No, you are not penalized for initial pull-ups, but an excessive number will count as errors
choice_b: Yes, every pull-up counts as an automatic error
choice_c: No, pull-ups are never counted or scored
choice_d: Yes, but only on Exercise 4
explanation: The manual states you will not be penalized for initial pull-ups; however, an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Pull-ups

question: Does stopping the vehicle without changing direction count as a pull-up?
choice_a: Yes, any stop during a backing exercise counts as a pull-up
choice_b: No, stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up
choice_c: Yes, but only if you stop for more than 5 seconds
choice_d: It counts as a back-up instead
explanation: The manual explicitly states that stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Pull-ups

question: Who is responsible for scoring the number of times you pull up during an exercise?
choice_a: You must self-report the count to the examiner
choice_b: It is automatically recorded by sensors in the alley cones
choice_c: The examiner
choice_d: It is not tracked, only the final position matters
explanation: The manual states the examiner will score the number of times you pull up.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Pull-ups

question: How is a 'back-up' defined in Basic Control Skills scoring?
choice_a: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment
choice_b: Exiting the vehicle during a forward exercise
choice_c: Sounding the horn before completing an exercise
choice_d: Backing up on a forward-moving exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position
explanation: The manual defines a back-up as backing up on a forward-moving exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Back-ups

question: On which exercise are back-ups scored?
choice_a: Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking
choice_b: Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing
choice_c: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop
choice_d: Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
explanation: The manual states back-ups will be scored on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Back-ups

question: How many free back-ups are you allowed on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: One free back-up
choice_b: None - there are no free back-ups on this exercise
choice_c: Two free back-ups
choice_d: Unlimited, as long as you stay within boundaries
explanation: The manual states there are NO free back-ups on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: Who scores the number of times you back up during Exercise 3?
choice_a: You count and report it yourself
choice_b: It is not scored, only encroachments matter
choice_c: The examiner
choice_d: A second examiner stationed at the far end of the alley
explanation: The manual states the examiner will score the number of times you back up.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Back-ups

question: How is an 'encroachment' defined during Basic Control Skills exercises?
choice_a: Failing to sound the horn upon completion of an exercise
choice_b: Exiting the vehicle more times than allowed
choice_c: Stopping outside the designated stop box
choice_d: Crossing over or touching an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of the vehicle, other than the mirrors or unique vehicle parts at or above door mirror height
explanation: The manual defines an encroachment as crossing over or touching a boundary line or cone with any portion of the vehicle other than the mirrors or unique vehicle parts at door mirror height or higher.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Encroachments

question: Do the vehicle's mirrors count as an encroachment if they cross a boundary line or cone?
choice_a: No, mirrors are excluded from encroachment scoring
choice_b: Yes, mirrors always count as encroachments
choice_c: Only side mirrors count, not door mirrors
choice_d: Only if the mirror physically touches a cone
explanation: The manual excludes the vehicle's mirrors (door or fender) from encroachment scoring.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Encroachments

question: A bucket truck's boom is a unique vehicle part positioned higher than the door mirrors. If it crosses a boundary line, is it scored as an encroachment?
choice_a: Yes, all unique vehicle parts count as encroachments regardless of height
choice_b: No, unique vehicle parts at or above door mirror height, such as a bucket truck's boom, are excluded from encroachment scoring
choice_c: Only if the examiner specifically points it out beforehand
choice_d: Yes, but it only counts as half an encroachment
explanation: The manual excludes unique vehicle parts at door mirror height or higher, such as a bucket truck, from encroachment scoring, while unique parts below door mirror height do count.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Encroachments

question: What must you do if you encroach on a boundary line or cone during an exercise?
choice_a: Continue the exercise and correct the position at the end
choice_b: Immediately exit the vehicle to inspect the encroachment
choice_c: Stop immediately when signaled by the examiner and return the vehicle within the exercise boundaries
choice_d: Sound the horn twice and wait for further instructions
explanation: The manual states if you encroach, the examiner will stop you and you must return the vehicle within the exercise boundaries, stopping immediately when signaled.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Encroachments

question: How does the examiner score encroachments?
choice_a: By deducting points only for the first encroachment
choice_b: Encroachments are not individually counted, only noted as pass/fail
choice_c: By measuring the distance the vehicle traveled outside the boundary
choice_d: By counting the number of times you touch or cross over an exercise boundary line or cone, with each encroachment counting as an error
explanation: The manual states the examiner will score the number of times you touch or cross over an exercise boundary line or cone, and each encroachment counts as an error.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Encroachments

question: How is a 'look' defined during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Exiting the vehicle while performing the exercise to check the vehicle's external position while backing
choice_b: Checking your mirrors without exiting the vehicle
choice_c: Asking the examiner for clarification on instructions
choice_d: Turning your head to check blind spots while driving forward
explanation: The manual defines a look as exiting the vehicle while performing an exercise to check the vehicle's position while backing.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Looks

question: What must you do before exiting the vehicle to take a 'look' during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Turn off the engine completely
choice_b: Set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral
choice_c: Sound the horn three times
choice_d: Radio the examiner for permission
explanation: The manual requires setting the parking brake(s) and placing the vehicle in neutral before safely exiting to take a look.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Looks

question: How many free looks are you allowed on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: None - all looks count as errors
choice_b: Two (2) free looks
choice_c: One (1) free look
choice_d: Three (3) free looks
explanation: The manual allows a maximum of one (1) free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Looks

question: How many free looks are you allowed on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: One (1) free look
choice_b: None - all looks count as errors
choice_c: Three (3) free looks
choice_d: Two (2) free looks
explanation: The manual allows a maximum of two (2) free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Looks

question: What may result if you do not safely secure the vehicle or safely exit/enter the vehicle while taking a look?
choice_a: An automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_b: A single error added to your score
choice_c: A verbal warning with no scoring penalty
choice_d: Loss of one free look only
explanation: The manual states failing to safely secure or safely exit/enter the vehicle may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Looks

question: On which two exercises is final vehicle position scored?
choice_a: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop and Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking
choice_b: Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
choice_c: All four exercises
choice_d: Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking only
explanation: The manual states final position is scored on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Final Position

question: What is required of your vehicle's final position, aside from mirrors and unique vehicle parts higher than the door mirrors?
choice_a: It must be centered exactly in the middle of the alley
choice_b: It must be parked with the engine off
choice_c: It must be within the final exercise boundaries as instructed by the examiner
choice_d: It must be positioned within 1 foot of the starting point
explanation: The manual states your vehicle must be within final exercise boundaries other than mirrors and unique vehicle parts higher than the door mirrors.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Final Position

question: What happens if you do not maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described by the examiner?
choice_a: You are given a second attempt at no penalty
choice_b: You lose only one free look
choice_c: Nothing, final position is only advisory
choice_d: You will be penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test
explanation: The manual states that if you do not maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described, you will be penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Final Position

topic: Failure to Follow Instructions / Unsafe Act
question: What may result from failing to follow the examiner's instructions for completing an exercise as directed?
choice_a: An automatic failure, and the test may be terminated by the examiner
choice_b: A single error added to your score with no further consequence
choice_c: A warning followed by a chance to redo the exercise
choice_d: Loss of all free pull-ups for the remaining exercises
explanation: The manual states failure to follow examiner instructions may result in an automatic failure and the test may be terminated.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Failure to Follow Instructions or Unsafe Act

topic: Failure to Follow Instructions / Unsafe Act
question: What should you do if you do not understand the examiner's instructions for an exercise?
choice_a: Proceed with your best guess to avoid delaying the test
choice_b: Ask the examiner for clarification
choice_c: Ask a passenger or bystander for help
choice_d: Automatically fail rather than risk an unsafe act
explanation: The manual instructs you to ask the examiner for clarification if you do not understand the instructions or how to complete the exercise.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Failure to Follow Instructions or Unsafe Act

topic: Failure to Follow Instructions / Unsafe Act
question: Which of the following is given as an example of an 'unsafe act' that may cause automatic failure?
choice_a: Taking slightly longer than average to complete an exercise
choice_b: Asking the examiner a clarifying question
choice_c: Forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while the vehicle is in motion
choice_d: Using a free look on Exercise 4
explanation: The manual gives forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion as examples of an unsafe act that may cause automatic failure.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Failure to Follow Instructions or Unsafe Act

topic: Failure to Follow Instructions / Unsafe Act
question: According to Section 12M, what is described as the highest priority during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Completing all four exercises within a time limit
choice_b: Minimizing the number of pull-ups
choice_c: Achieving a perfect final position on every exercise
choice_d: Safety of the driver, the examiner, and the testing area
explanation: The manual states safety of the driver, the examiner, and the testing area is of the highest priority.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Failure to Follow Instructions or Unsafe Act

topic: Failure to Follow Instructions / Unsafe Act
question: If permitted, what may you ask the examiner to do before beginning an exercise?
choice_a: Walk you through the exercise area
choice_b: Demonstrate the exercise by driving it themselves
choice_c: Extend the time limit for the exercise
choice_d: Waive the free pull-up or free look allowance
explanation: The manual notes that, if permitted, you may ask the examiner to walk you through the exercise area.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.1 Scoring - Failure to Follow Instructions or Unsafe Act

question: What does Exercise 1 - Forward Stop demonstrate?
choice_a: Your ability to back a vehicle in a straight line
choice_b: Your ability to judge the front of your vehicle during a controlled stop
choice_c: Your ability to maneuver around objects while moving forward
choice_d: Your ability to offset back and park a vehicle
explanation: The manual states Exercise 1 demonstrates your ability to judge the front of your vehicle during a controlled stop.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, where must the front most part of your vehicle stop?
choice_a: As close as possible to the stop box without a specific boundary
choice_b: Exactly on the outer boundary line
choice_c: Within the stop box at the end of the alley, without going past it
choice_d: At least one vehicle length before the stop box
explanation: The manual requires stopping with the front most part of the vehicle within the box at the end of the alley without going past it.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: How many times may you stop during Exercise 1 - Forward Stop?
choice_a: As many times as needed to get it right
choice_b: Twice, with the second stop being scored
choice_c: There is no limit specified
choice_d: Only once
explanation: The manual states you may stop only once during Exercise 1 - Forward Stop.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: What does the examiner do before you begin Exercise 1 - Forward Stop?
choice_a: Points out the front most part of your vehicle
choice_b: Demonstrates the stop by driving the alley first
choice_c: Places a cone at the exact stopping point
choice_d: Measures your vehicle's total length
explanation: The manual states your examiner will point out the front most part of your vehicle when giving instructions for this exercise.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: After stopping in Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, what must you do before the examiner scores the exercise?
choice_a: Turn off the engine and exit the vehicle
choice_b: Set your parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound the horn
choice_c: Wait for the examiner to approach the vehicle window
choice_d: Flash your headlights twice
explanation: The manual instructs that once stopped, you set your parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound the horn so the examiner can score the exercise.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: In scoring Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, when do you receive points?
choice_a: If you stop within exactly 6 inches of the stop box line
choice_b: If you complete the stop in under 10 seconds
choice_c: If the front most part of the vehicle (other than unique vehicle parts higher than the door mirrors) is not in the stop box
choice_d: If you use a free pull-up during the stop
explanation: The manual states you will receive points if the front most part of the vehicle, other than unique vehicle parts higher than the door mirrors, is not in the stop box.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: What does Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing demonstrate?
choice_a: Your ability to judge the front of your vehicle during a stop
choice_b: Your ability to offset back and park at the end of an alley
choice_c: Your ability to track around objects while moving forward
choice_d: Your ability to back a vehicle in a straight line
explanation: The manual states Exercise 2 demonstrates your ability to back a vehicle in a straight line.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: How does Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing begin?
choice_a: From your stopped position from the previous exercise, the examiner asks you to pull forward and stop when they raise their hand
choice_b: You start already positioned at the far end of the alley
choice_c: The examiner drives the vehicle to the starting point
choice_d: You begin by sounding the horn and setting the parking brake
explanation: The manual states that from your stopped position from the previous exercise, the examiner will ask you to pull forward and stop when they raise their hand.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: In Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, how far must you back the vehicle?
choice_a: Until the rear of the vehicle touches the starting cones
choice_b: Straight through the alley until the front of your vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end
choice_c: A fixed distance of 100 feet regardless of alley length
choice_d: Until the examiner signals with the horn
explanation: The manual instructs you to back straight through the alley until the front of your vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: Which three things are scored on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: Back-ups, looks, and forward tracking clearance
choice_b: Encroachments and time only
choice_c: Pull-ups, encroachments, and final position
choice_d: Pull-ups and back-ups only
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for pull-ups, encroachments, and final position on this exercise.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: How many free pull-ups and free vehicle exits are you allowed on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: Two (2) free pull-ups and two (2) safe exits
choice_b: No free pull-ups but one (1) safe exit
choice_c: One (1) free pull-up and no allowed exits
choice_d: One (1) free pull-up and one (1) safe exit to check around the vehicle
explanation: The manual states you are allowed one free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one time to check around it.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: How do you signal that you have completed Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: Set your parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound your horn
choice_b: Flash your headlights and wait for the examiner
choice_c: Exit the vehicle and stand beside it
choice_d: Simply come to a stop; no additional signal is required
explanation: The manual instructs that when you have completed the exercise, you set your parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound your horn to inform the examiner.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: What does Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking demonstrate?
choice_a: Your ability to back a vehicle in a straight line
choice_b: Your ability to maneuver a vehicle around other objects while moving forward
choice_c: Your ability to judge the front of your vehicle during a stop
choice_d: Your ability to offset back and park a vehicle
explanation: The manual states Exercise 3 demonstrates your ability to maneuver a vehicle around other objects while moving forward.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, what must you keep between the cone and the line while driving forward through the opening?
choice_a: Your left most front tire
choice_b: The center of the vehicle's front bumper
choice_c: Your right most rear tire
choice_d: Your right most front tire
explanation: The manual instructs you to keep the right most rear tire between the cone and the line without stopping.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: Which three things are scored on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Pull-ups, encroachments, and final position
choice_b: Looks, pull-ups, and final position
choice_c: Encroachments and looks only
choice_d: Back-ups, encroachments, and forward tracking clearance
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for back-ups, encroachments, and forward tracking clearance on this exercise.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: Are you permitted to exit the vehicle during Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: No, you are not permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise
choice_b: Yes, up to one free exit is allowed
choice_c: Yes, up to two free exits are allowed
choice_d: Yes, but only after completing the offset
explanation: The manual explicitly states you are NOT permitted to exit the vehicle during Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: Where must you stop your vehicle at the end of Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Anywhere within the opposite lane, as long as you are stopped
choice_b: Parallel to the outer boundary, prior to or at the cones at the far end of the exercise
choice_c: At a 45-degree angle to the boundary line
choice_d: Exactly where you first steered left through the opening
explanation: The manual instructs you to stop your vehicle when parallel to the outer boundary, prior to or at the cones at the far end of the exercise.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: How do you signal that you have completed Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Exit the vehicle and wave to the examiner
choice_b: Flash your hazard lights
choice_c: Set your parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound your horn
choice_d: Simply wait silently for the examiner to approach
explanation: The manual instructs you to set your parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound your horn to inform the examiner you have completed the exercise.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: What does Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing demonstrate?
choice_a: Your ability to judge the front of your vehicle during a stop
choice_b: Your ability to track around objects while moving forward
choice_c: Your ability to back a vehicle in a perfectly straight line only
choice_d: Your ability to offset back and park a vehicle at the end of an alley
explanation: The manual states Exercise 4 demonstrates your ability to offset back and park a vehicle at the end of an alley.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: In Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, how close must the rear most part of your vehicle come to the rear of the alley?
choice_a: Within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley
choice_b: Within one (1) foot of the rear of the alley
choice_c: Within six (6) feet of the rear of the alley
choice_d: Touching the rear boundary line exactly
explanation: The manual states you must bring the rear most part of your vehicle within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: What must be true of your vehicle's orientation within the alley when Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing is completed?
choice_a: The vehicle may be at any angle as long as it's within boundaries
choice_b: The vehicle must be straight within the alley
choice_c: The vehicle must be angled toward the outer boundary
choice_d: The vehicle must be perpendicular to the alley

source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: In Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, what restriction applies to the outer boundary line?
choice_a: You must touch the outer boundary line at least once
choice_b: The outer boundary line only applies to Exercise 3
choice_c: You may not go beyond the outer boundary line
choice_d: There is no outer boundary restriction in this exercise
explanation: The manual states you may not go beyond the outer boundary line during this exercise.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: Which three things are scored on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: Back-ups, looks, and forward tracking clearance
choice_b: Encroachments and time only
choice_c: Pull-ups and looks only
choice_d: Pull-ups, encroachments, and final position

source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual Supplement, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, 12M.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: Two (2) free pull-ups and up to two (2) exits to check around the vehicle
choice_b: One (1) free pull-up and one (1) exit
choice_c: Two (2) free pull-ups but no exits permitted

question: According to Section 13, what must you do at all times during the On-Road Driving test?
choice_a: Maintain a constant speed at the posted limit
choice_b: Drive in a safe and responsible manner
choice_c: Keep both hands off the wheel while shifting
choice_d: Follow only the examiner's verbal cues, ignoring traffic signs
explanation: The manual states that at all times during the test, you must drive in a safe and responsible manner.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: Which of the following is explicitly required of you during the On-Road Driving test, per Section 13?
choice_a: Complete the route in under 30 minutes
choice_b: Use only automatic transmission vehicles
choice_c: Wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs/signals/laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation
choice_d: Avoid using turn signals unless requested by the examiner
explanation: The manual requires that you wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: During the driving test, what is the examiner scoring you on?
choice_a: Only your final parking maneuver
choice_b: Only your knowledge of road signs
choice_c: Only whether you exceed the speed limit
choice_d: Specific driving maneuvers as well as your general driving behavior
explanation: The manual states the examiner will be scoring you on specific driving maneuvers as well as on your general driving behavior.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: Will you be asked to drive in an unsafe manner during the On-Road Driving test?
choice_a: No, you will not be asked to drive in an unsafe manner
choice_b: Yes, if the examiner needs to test your emergency reactions
choice_c: Only during the expressway portion of the test
choice_d: Yes, but only in low-traffic conditions
explanation: The manual states you will not be asked to drive in an unsafe manner.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: What happens if your test route does not include a certain traffic situation, such as a railroad crossing?
choice_a: That portion of the test is skipped entirely with no penalty
choice_b: You may be asked to simulate the situation by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing
choice_c: You automatically receive full credit for that maneuver
choice_d: The test is rescheduled to a route that includes it
explanation: The manual states that if your route lacks certain traffic situations, you may be asked to simulate them by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: As you approach a turn, what must you do regarding your gears and speed?
choice_a: Come to a complete stop before every turn regardless of traffic
choice_b: Accelerate through the turn to maintain momentum
choice_c: Slow down smoothly, change gears as needed to keep power, but do not coast unsafely
choice_d: Shift into neutral early to conserve fuel
explanation: The manual instructs you to slow down smoothly and change gears as needed to keep power, without coasting unsafely.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: How does the manual define 'unsafe coasting'?
choice_a: Any time the vehicle travels more than one car length without braking
choice_b: Coasting downhill at any speed
choice_c: Shifting gears more than twice within an intersection
choice_d: When your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as the vehicle being out of gear, with the clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral, for more than the length of your vehicle.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: If stopping behind another vehicle before a turn, where should you stop?
choice_a: Where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you (a safe gap)
choice_b: As close as possible to the vehicle ahead to save space
choice_c: At least three full car lengths back regardless of visibility
choice_d: Wherever the examiner points, with no other guidance given
explanation: The manual states that if stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of you, maintaining a safe gap.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: While waiting to make a turn, what should you do with your front wheels?
choice_a: Turn them slightly toward the direction of the turn
choice_b: Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead
choice_c: Turn them away from oncoming traffic
choice_d: It does not matter as long as the vehicle is stopped
explanation: The manual instructs you to keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead while stopped and waiting to turn.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: During the turn itself, what should you keep checking to ensure the vehicle does not hit anything?
choice_a: The speedometer
choice_b: The examiner's face for reactions
choice_c: Your mirror, to make sure the vehicle does not hit anything on the inside of the turn
choice_d: The clock, to ensure the turn isn't taking too long
explanation: The manual instructs you to keep checking your mirror during the turn to make sure the vehicle does not hit anything on the inside of the turn.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: After completing a turn, what should you do regarding lane position?
choice_a: Remain in the leftmost lane for at least one block
choice_b: Immediately change lanes without signaling
choice_c: Come to a full stop to check your position
choice_d: Get up to the speed of traffic, use your turn signal, and move into the right-most lane when safe to do so (if not already there)
explanation: The manual instructs that after the turn, you should get up to speed, use your turn signal, and move into the right-most lane when safe to do so.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: As you approach an intersection, what should you do if you must come to a complete stop?
choice_a: Come to a complete stop (no coasting) behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front of you
choice_b: Coast to a gradual stop to save brake wear
choice_c: Stop only if a pedestrian is visibly present
choice_d: Roll slowly forward until traffic allows you through
explanation: The manual instructs that if necessary, you should come to a complete stop, without coasting, behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: While driving through an intersection, what must you avoid doing?
choice_a: Checking your mirrors
choice_b: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_c: Decelerating for pedestrians
choice_d: Keeping your hands on the wheel
explanation: The manual states you must not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: While stopped at an intersection, what must your vehicle not do?
choice_a: Idle for more than 10 seconds
choice_b: Have its turn signal active
choice_c: Roll forward or backward
choice_d: Remain in gear with the clutch engaged
explanation: The manual states your vehicle must not roll forward or backward while stopped at an intersection.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: Once through an intersection, what should you do?
choice_a: Immediately return to the leftmost lane
choice_b: Turn off your headlights if it is daytime
choice_c: Signal a lane change regardless of need
choice_d: Continue checking mirrors and traffic, and accelerate smoothly, changing gears as necessary
explanation: The manual instructs that once through the intersection, you should continue checking mirrors and traffic and accelerate smoothly, changing gears as necessary.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: During the Urban Business portion of the test, what following-distance expectation applies?
choice_a: You are expected to make regular traffic checks and maintain a safe following distance
choice_b: Following distance is not evaluated in urban areas
choice_c: You must maintain exactly two car lengths at all times
choice_d: Following distance only matters above 35 mph
explanation: The manual states you are expected to make regular traffic checks and maintain a safe following distance during the Urban Business portion.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: Where should your vehicle be positioned during the Urban Business portion of the test?
choice_a: As far left as safely possible
choice_b: Centered in the proper (right-most) lane
choice_c: Straddling the center line for visibility
choice_d: In whichever lane has the least traffic
explanation: The manual states your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane, which is the right-most lane.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: What speed expectation applies during the Urban Business portion of the test?
choice_a: Drive at least 5 mph under the posted limit at all times
choice_b: Match the speed of the fastest vehicle on the road
choice_c: Keep up with the flow of traffic but do not exceed the posted speed limit
choice_d: Speed is not evaluated in urban business areas
explanation: The manual states you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: During multiple-lane portions of the test, what lane change maneuver will you be asked to perform?
choice_a: Change lanes only to the right
choice_b: Weave between three lanes consecutively
choice_c: Change lanes only while braking
choice_d: Change lanes to the left, and then back to the right
explanation: The manual states you will be asked to change lanes to the left, and then back to the right, during multiple lane portions of the test.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.4 Lane Changes

question: What is the correct procedure for making a lane change during the test?
choice_a: Make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so
choice_b: Signal first, then check traffic while already moving into the new lane
choice_c: Change lanes quickly to minimize time spent signaling
choice_d: Change lanes without signaling if no vehicles are visible
explanation: The manual instructs you to make necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when safe.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.4 Lane Changes

question: Before entering the expressway, what must you do?
choice_a: Come to a complete stop at the entrance ramp
choice_b: Check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic
choice_c: Accelerate to maximum speed before merging
choice_d: Wait for the examiner's explicit verbal go-ahead
explanation: The manual instructs you to check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic before entering the expressway.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: Once on the expressway, what must you maintain?
choice_a: The leftmost lane at all times for passing
choice_b: A fixed distance of exactly 200 feet from all vehicles
choice_c: Proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed, while continuing to check traffic thoroughly
choice_d: Maximum legal speed regardless of traffic flow
explanation: The manual states that once on the expressway, you must maintain proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed, and continue checking traffic thoroughly.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: When exiting the expressway, what should you do?
choice_a: Decelerate while still in the main travel lanes before entering the exit lane
choice_b: Signal only after entering the exit lane
choice_c: Maintain highway speed until the last possible moment
choice_d: Make necessary traffic checks, use proper signals, and decelerate smoothly in the exit lane
explanation: The manual instructs you to make necessary traffic checks, use proper signals, and decelerate smoothly in the exit lane when exiting the expressway.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: Once on the exit ramp, what must you continue to do?
choice_a: Continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles
choice_b: Accelerate back to highway speed in case you missed the exit
choice_c: Straddle the lane markings to maximize visibility
choice_d: Come to a complete stop immediately upon entering the ramp
explanation: The manual states that once on the exit ramp, you must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: What is the Stop/Start maneuver meant to simulate?
choice_a: An emergency roadside breakdown requiring a tow
choice_b: Pulling the vehicle over to the side of the road and stopping as if you were going to get out and check something on your vehicle
choice_c: A routine fuel stop
choice_d: A driver's license checkpoint
explanation: The manual describes this maneuver as pulling over to the side of the road and stopping as if you were going to get out and check something on your vehicle.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: As you prepare for the Stop/Start maneuver, what is the correct sequence of actions?
choice_a: Brake hard immediately, then check traffic afterward
choice_b: Activate your left turn signal and coast to a stop
choice_c: Check traffic, activate your right turn signal, decelerate smoothly and brake evenly, changing gears as necessary, then bring the vehicle to a full stop without coasting
choice_d: Sound the horn, then signal, then brake
explanation: The manual describes checking traffic, activating the right turn signal, decelerating smoothly and braking evenly with gear changes as necessary, then stopping fully without coasting.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: Once stopped during the Stop/Start maneuver, which of the following is required?
choice_a: Leave the engine running in gear with your foot on the brake
choice_b: Keep the turn signal active until you resume driving
choice_c: Exit the vehicle immediately to inspect it
choice_d: Vehicle parallel to the curb or shoulder, out of the traffic flow, not blocking driveways/hydrants/etc., with turn signal canceled, four-way flashers on, parking brake applied, and gearshift in neutral or park
explanation: The manual lists these exact requirements once stopped: parallel to the curb, out of traffic flow, not blocking driveways/hydrants, signal canceled, flashers on, parking brake applied, and neutral or park.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When instructed to resume from the Stop/Start maneuver, what should you check first?
choice_a: Traffic and your mirrors thoroughly in all directions
choice_b: The fuel gauge
choice_c: The parking brake indicator light only
choice_d: Nothing; you should pull out immediately once instructed
explanation: The manual instructs that when resuming, you should check traffic and your mirrors thoroughly in all directions.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When resuming from the Stop/Start maneuver, what should you do with the steering wheel before the vehicle moves?
choice_a: Turn it fully toward traffic to prepare for merging
choice_b: Do not turn the wheel before your vehicle moves
choice_c: Turn it away from traffic to widen your view
choice_d: It does not matter as long as you check mirrors
explanation: The manual explicitly instructs that you should not turn the wheel before your vehicle moves when resuming.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When resuming from the Stop/Start maneuver, which direction should you especially check traffic from?
choice_a: The right
choice_b: Directly behind only
choice_c: The left
choice_d: Directly ahead only
explanation: The manual states you should check traffic from all directions, especially to the left, when resuming.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: After your vehicle is back in the flow of traffic following the Stop/Start maneuver, what should you do?
choice_a: Reactivate your four-way flashers
choice_b: Sound your horn to signal completion
choice_c: Immediately change to the leftmost lane
choice_d: Cancel your left turn signal
explanation: The manual states that once your vehicle is back in the flow of traffic, you should cancel your left turn signal.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: Before entering a curve, what should you do regarding speed?
choice_a: Reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_b: Brake continuously throughout the curve
choice_c: Accelerate to maintain momentum through the curve
choice_d: Downshift only after entering the curve
explanation: The manual instructs you to reduce speed before entering a curve so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.7 Curve

question: While driving through a curve, what should you continue doing?
choice_a: Straddle the center line for better visibility
choice_b: Keep the vehicle in the lane and continue checking traffic in all directions
choice_c: Focus only on the road surface directly ahead
choice_d: Accelerate gradually to exit the curve faster
explanation: The manual instructs you to keep the vehicle in the lane and continue checking traffic in all directions while in a curve.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.7 Curve

question: Before reaching a railroad crossing, what should all commercial drivers do?
choice_a: Come to a complete stop regardless of visible train activity
choice_b: Accelerate to clear the crossing quickly
choice_c: Decelerate, brake smoothly, shift gears as necessary, look and listen for trains, and check traffic in all directions
choice_d: Sound the horn continuously until past the crossing
explanation: The manual instructs all commercial drivers to decelerate, brake smoothly, shift gears as necessary, look and listen for trains, and check traffic before reaching a crossing.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: What must you not do while any part of your vehicle is in a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Keep both hands on the steering wheel
choice_b: Look and listen for approaching trains
choice_c: Check mirrors and traffic
choice_d: Stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes
explanation: The manual states you must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: If you are driving a bus, school bus, or a vehicle displaying placards, how far from the nearest rail must you stop at a railroad crossing (unless the crossing is exempt)?
choice_a: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
choice_b: Within 25 feet but not less than 5 feet from the nearest rail
choice_c: Exactly 100 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: As close as possible without touching the rail
explanation: The manual requires these vehicles to stop within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: As a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle approaches a railroad crossing, what should be activated?
choice_a: The stop arm and red warning lights
choice_b: The four-way flashers
choice_c: The headlights on high beam
choice_d: The rear hazard lights only
explanation: The manual states that as the vehicle approaches a railroad crossing, the driver should activate the four-way flashers.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: When must a bus operator deactivate the four-way flashers at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Before beginning to decelerate for the crossing
choice_b: As soon as the vehicle stops before the crossing
choice_c: After the vehicle crosses the tracks
choice_d: They should remain on for the rest of the route
explanation: The manual states four-way flashers should be deactivated after the vehicle crosses the tracks.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: What should you do if your test route does not include a railroad crossing?
choice_a: That portion of the test is automatically skipped with no discussion
choice_b: You are given a written quiz on railroad safety instead
choice_c: The test is rescheduled to a different route
choice_d: You may be asked to explain and demonstrate the proper railroad crossing procedures to the examiner at a simulated location
explanation: The manual states that not all routes have a railroad crossing, and you may be asked to explain and demonstrate proper procedures at a simulated location.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass during the road test, what might the examiner ask you?
choice_a: What the posted clearance or height was
choice_b: What the speed limit was five miles back
choice_c: How many vehicles passed under it with you
choice_d: What the name of the overpass was
explanation: The manual states you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was after driving under an overpass.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: After going over a bridge during the road test, what might the examiner ask you?
choice_a: What the posted clearance was
choice_b: What the posted weight limit was
choice_c: How long the bridge was
choice_d: What year the bridge was built
explanation: The manual states you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted weight limit was after going over a bridge.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: If your test route has no bridge or overpass, what might you be asked instead?
choice_a: Nothing; that portion of scoring is skipped entirely
choice_b: To describe a bridge from memory
choice_c: To identify and explain another traffic sign that may appear on the route
choice_d: To draw a diagram of a typical overpass
explanation: The manual states that if your route has no bridge or overpass, you may be asked about another traffic sign that may appear on the route.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: Who is required to demonstrate a student discharge during the road test?
choice_a: All CDL Class B applicants
choice_b: Only applicants using a manual transmission bus
choice_c: All applicants regardless of endorsement sought
choice_d: Applicants for a School Bus endorsement
explanation: The manual states that if you are applying for a School Bus endorsement, you will be required to demonstrate a student discharge.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: As you approach the student pick-up during a student discharge, what must you do?
choice_a: Decelerate and approach at a slow rate of speed while continuing to check traffic, activate amber warning lights and right turn signal, move as far right as possible, and recheck traffic
choice_b: Activate red warning lights and the stop arm before you begin decelerating
choice_c: Come to an immediate stop as soon as students are visible
choice_d: Sound the horn continuously while approaching
explanation: The manual describes decelerating and approaching slowly while checking traffic, activating amber lights and the right turn signal, moving right, and rechecking traffic.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: How far away from students at the stop must a school bus come to a complete stop during student discharge?
choice_a: At least 5 feet away
choice_b: At least 10 feet away from students
choice_c: At least 25 feet away
choice_d: At least 50 feet away
explanation: The manual states the bus must come to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: When resuming from a student discharge, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Sound the horn twice before pulling away
choice_b: Wait exactly 30 seconds before proceeding
choice_c: Check all mirrors, turn off warning lights and the stop arm, close the door, check traffic, and accelerate away from the stop area
choice_d: Leave the stop arm extended until fully back in traffic
explanation: The manual lists checking all mirrors, turning off warning lights and the stop arm, closing the door, checking traffic, and accelerating away as the resume procedure.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: What is required regarding clutch usage when shifting?
choice_a: Use the clutch only when downshifting
choice_b: Avoid the clutch when possible to save wear
choice_c: Use the clutch only above 20 mph
choice_d: Always use the clutch to shift
explanation: The manual states you should always use the clutch to shift.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: If your vehicle has an unsynchronized manual transmission, what must you do when shifting?
choice_a: Double-clutch
choice_b: Single-clutch and rev the engine between shifts
choice_c: Avoid shifting gears entirely during the test
choice_d: Use the clutch only when coming to a stop
explanation: The manual states that if equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, you must double-clutch when shifting.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Which of the following clutch behaviors is prohibited during the road test?
choice_a: Fully depressing the clutch during every gear change
choice_b: Riding the clutch to control speed, coasting with the clutch depressed, or 'popping' the clutch
choice_c: Releasing the clutch smoothly after a shift
choice_d: Using the clutch to start the vehicle moving from a stop
explanation: The manual prohibits riding the clutch to control speed, coasting with the clutch depressed, or 'popping' the clutch.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Which gear-related behavior is prohibited during the road test?
choice_a: Selecting a gear that avoids revving or lugging the engine
choice_b: Shifting smoothly between gears
choice_c: Grinding or clashing gears
choice_d: Downshifting before a stop
explanation: The manual prohibits grinding or clashing gears.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: What kind of gear should you select while driving during the test?
choice_a: The highest gear available regardless of engine load
choice_b: The lowest gear available at all times
choice_c: Whichever gear matches your speed exactly, regardless of engine strain
choice_d: One that does not rev or lug the engine
explanation: The manual instructs you to select a gear that does not rev or lug the engine.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Where should you avoid shifting gears during the road test?
choice_a: In turns and intersections
choice_b: On straightaways
choice_c: On expressway on-ramps
choice_d: While stopped at a red light

question: Which braking behaviors are prohibited during the road test?
choice_a: Using steady, smooth brake pressure
choice_b: Riding or pumping the brake, and braking harshly

choice_d: Covering the brake pedal near intersections
explanation: The manual prohibits riding or pumping the brake, and braking harshly.
source_note: New Hampshire Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.13(c) Brake Usage

question: What is the correct braking technique described in Section 13?
choice_a: Pump the brakes repeatedly to signal other drivers
choice_b: Apply maximum brake pressure immediately, then release
choice_c: Brake smoothly using steady pressure
choice_d: Ride the brake lightly through curves
explanation: The manual states the correct technique is to brake smoothly using steady pressure.

question: Which of the following is prohibited under the Lane Usage behavior category?
choice_a: Stopping behind stop lines, crosswalks, or stop signs

choice_c: Moving to or remaining in the right-most lane unless it is blocked
choice_d: Putting the vehicle over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings
explanation: The manual prohibits putting the vehicle over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings under the Lane Usage category.

question: Where should a left turn on a multiple-lane road be completed?
choice_a: In the lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_b: In the leftmost lane on the far side of the road
choice_c: In any lane, as long as it is a legal turn
choice_d: In the same lane you started the turn from

question: Where should a right turn be completed?
choice_a: In the center lane of a multi-lane road
choice_b: In the right-most (curb) lane
choice_c: In whichever lane has less traffic
choice_d: In the lane closest to oncoming traffic

question: Under general lane usage expectations, which lane should you move to or remain in unless it is blocked?

choice_b: The left-most lane
choice_c: The right-most lane

question: What steering behavior is the driver expected to avoid?

question: When should you keep both hands on the steering wheel?

question: Besides checking traffic, what else should you check regularly during the road test?
